text: Besides insects, stored rice is vulnerable to rodents and birds. The source names three common rodent species found around stored rice: the black/roof rat, common around houses (ក្ណារជុំ ពណ៌ខ្មៅ ឬ ក្ណារជុំតាមផ្ទះ, Rattus rattus), the Norway rat (ក្ណារ Norwegian, Rattus norvegicus), and the house mouse (ក្ណារតូចៗតាមផ្ទះ, Mus musculus). Beyond eating and contaminating grain with droppings and hair, rodents damage storage bags, bins, and building structures, and their presence can spread further as populations grow if left unmanaged. Control approaches described include: physical exclusion — for example, smooth disc-shaped rat guards (ដុំបារ / rat guards) fitted around the legs of raised granaries or storehouses so rodents cannot climb up from the ground; traps; cats; and poison bait, used carefully and away from areas where it could contaminate stored food or reach children, pets, or non-target animals. General sanitation matters as much as any single tool: keeping the storage area free of spilled grain, clutter, and overgrown vegetation around the building removes the food and shelter that attract rodents in the first place, and is described as more effective over time than reactive control alone. For birds, the source recommends fine netting or screening over storage openings to physically exclude them, since bird droppings and feeding both contaminate and reduce stored grain. (Note: specific rodent-control product names and dosages are not detailed here in line with general safety practice — follow current label instructions and local agricultural extension guidance for any poison bait product actually used.)
